title: Instrumented canary + heartbeat metrics to reveal console ingress visibility gaps
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: A recent capacity regression in eu-west-1 surfaced a blindspot: the console ingress pipeline showed no reliable short-interval liveness signals and per-route queue depth histograms, which delayed identification of upstream throttling. This work creates a small, low-overhead synthetic canary + heartbeat metric surface that exercises the same ingress path as customer requests, captures prefix-latency and queue_depth histograms at 1s granularity, and ensures traces are sampled deterministically for canary requests. Goals: (1) detect regional backpressure within 30s, (2) correlate canary traces with tenant-level tail latency to reduce MTTI, (3) add dashboard panels and alerts, and (4) publish a runbook for on-call to triage ingress saturation incidents.
acceptance_criteria: A heartbeat counter metric (console.canary.heartbeat_total) incremented every 10s from canary job in each region
Histogram metrics for console.canary.prefix_latency_ms and console.ingress.queue_depth with 1s resolution visible in Grafana
A deterministic trace sampling flag for canary requests that forces 100% tracing for those synthetic requests
New Grafana dashboard with top-level canary health, regional latency heatmap, and queue_depth panels (link added)
Two alerts: (a) canary-heartbeat-missing > 30s and (b) queue_depth P95 > threshold for 3 minutes; properly routed to SRE
Runbook entry created with step-by-step triage and fallback (canary job restart, route failover, capacity escalation)
End-to-end tests in staging exercising canary and verifying metrics emitted; PRs merged and released in console-2026.02
tasks: T1: Add lightweight canary runner service (k8s cronjob) to hit /health and a synthetic route that mirrors customer ingress - owner: Diego Martinez - 2pt
T2: Instrument console ingress to emit console.ingress.queue_depth (gauge) and console.canary.prefix_latency_ms (histogram) - owner: Priya Nair - 2pt
T3: Wire canary requests to include x-canary-id and force trace sampling via x-trace-sample header - owner: Diego Martinez - 1pt
T4: Create Grafana dashboard & panels, import template JSON to dashboards repo - owner: Observability Team - 1pt
T5: Define alert rules and pager routing, add test alerts to staging - owner: SRE - 1pt
T6: Update runbook (Confluence) with play-by-play and automated remediation steps - owner: Ava Chen - 1pt
comments: 2026-01-10 - Ava Chen: Ticket created after postmortem of eu-west-1 capacity regression. Root cause: invisibility of short-lived queue pressure due to coarse scrape intervals and lack of synthetic liveness probes.

2026-01-12 - Diego Martinez: Spiked an early prototype in staging that emits canary.heartbeat_total every 10s. Verified metric ingestion but need to reduce label cardinality for tenant route to avoid TSDB blowup.

2026-01-14 - Priya Nair: Proposed histogram bucket set for prefix latency: [0.5,1,2,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000] ms. Trade-off: higher buckets increase series cardinality; kept coarse upper buckets to limit cardinality.

2026-01-18 - Observability Team: Dashboard draft available: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xyz123/canary-ingress-visibility. Panels include heartbeat timeline, per-region P95 prefix latency, and queue_depth heatmap.

2026-01-20 - SRE: Alert definitions staged in prometheus: canary_heartbeat_missing > 30s (severity=P1) and ingress_queue_depth_p95 > 50 (severity=P1). Need confirmation on thresholds from platform PM.
2026-01-22 - Platform PM (Lena Ortiz): Reviewed alerts; suggested raising queue_depth threshold to 75 for eu-west-1 due to observed baseline. Agreed to per-region thresholds.

2026-01-24 - Diego Martinez: PR opened for instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4923. Running integration tests in staging; found unexpected label cardinality from route_id — added coarse bucketing and route_group label instead.

2026-01-26 - QA: End-to-end staging test passed. Canary traces appear with x-canary-id and are linkable to heartbeat series in Grafana. Noted one false-positive alert in staging due to cronjob delayed pod restart; addressed by making cronjob TTL more resilient.

2026-01-28 - Ava Chen: Merged PR for dashboard JSON into dashboards repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dashboards/pull/811. Planning release in console-2026.02; follow-up for long-term retention and downsampling being tracked under ENG-118645.
